environment.description: Application deployed identically but the EC2 instance runs with a mandatory AppArmor profile (loaded in enforce mode) that confines the gunicorn process. The profile grants read-write access ONLY to /var/app/data/users.db and /tmp/*, denies all network-related syscalls except accept/recv/send on the bound socket, and critically uses a dbus-mediated SQLite access layer where the profile includes a rule 'deny /var/app/data/users.db w,' for any query execution path that does not originate from a prepared statement binding (the AppArmor profile hooks into the libsqlite3 shared library's sqlite3_exec vs sqlite3_prepare_v2 call paths via a custom LSM stacking module 'aa-sqlite-enforce' that intercepts VFS write operations and validates the query was constructed via the parameterized API). Additionally, the instance has an iptables OUTPUT chain rule that drops all packets to 169.254.169.254 (blocking SSRF to metadata), and the SQLite database file has an extended attribute (security.sqlite_ro_fallback=1) that triggers the aa-sqlite-enforce module to return SQLITE_READONLY when a non-parameterized DML statement modifies data.

config.lsm_policy: intercepts sqlite3_exec write path; allows writes only via sqlite3_prepare_v2 with bound parameters
config.net_restriction: deny all outbound except established connections on port 443
